THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE          39

[Photograph: Reproduction of a catalog page. Text reads:

Catalogue of Savoy College.

LOCATION.

Savoy is situated eleven miles west from Denison, in a healthy locality. Its people are largely and liberally educated, believing it their duty to educate at least their children, if not themselves.

FACULTY.

The Faculty of this college is composed of more than the average council of the students, consisting of more than one hundred students; and its results and public esteem toward their pupils have been greatly lauded by the same.

LITERARY SOCIETIES.

There are two literary societies connected with this College — the Fluvanna and the Athenian.

Board can be had at ten dollars per month. The Faculty have assured us that those desiring to board themselves can board themselves at from three to four dollars per month.

SAW HOUSTON HALL.

In addition to the large number of existing Main Streets on the ground, there will be a large building erected, at the expense of the Board of Trustees, as a dormitory for the Students—both Ladies and Gentlemen will be accommodated—it will contain at least one hall.

Our Faculty.

It is the object of the faculty to make the course of instruction not merely theoretical, but also practical. All those facilities for acquiring an education may be had at lower rates than anywhere else in this city, county, or any other county, state or other parts of Texas.

We aim to instruct students, practical, thorough work throughout.

In the future, as in the past, we shall labor with all our ability to assist our students to reach the goal of perfection, to our charges, and to arouse in them a love for learning and a desire to excel.]
notes: Printed page 39. Page is a reproduction of a catalog page describing Savoy College's location, faculty, literary societies, and facilities. The text is somewhat degraded.
